newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - Oil Search said "buy".
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - Oil Search said "buy".

text.p: Stockbroker Hartley Poynton issued a buy recommendation for Papua New Guinea based Oil Search Ltd, saying moves to increase production at the Kutubu oil field will maintain current earnings until the full impact in calendar 1998 of production at the new Gobe field.
In a research report, the broker said the start of the Gobe production would place Oil Search on a 1998 price earnings ratio of 12.2 times and a cashflow multiple of 4.2 times.
The report said measures implemented at Kutubu were expected to maintain 1997 production at 100,000 barrels a day, arresting a decline in Oil Search's 1997 earnings.
There was potential for production upside from Kutubu in 1997 through production upgrades and exploration, it said.

The Gobe field had the potential to provide further strength to 1997 earnings with first production late in the year a possibility, and a full year's production from Gobe in 1998 would almost double current Kutubu production, it said.
In addition, there was potential for production upside at Gobe in later years through increased reserve penetration.
Hartley Poynton said Oil Search represented an investment in excellent exploration acreage, and the broker was particularly excited about potential benefits from near-term exploration.
"The upcoming drilling programme illustrates this quality with eight wells targeting total possible reserves of over 1.5 billion barrels of oil," it said.
"Initial success from the Moran-1X well (in the Papua New Guinea highlands) represents a critical point for the company's next re-rating upwards," it said.
But the broker was critical of Oil Search's recent 10.1 percent acquisition of Discovery Petroleum NL.

While Oil Search's balance sheet was capable of digesting the buy, Hartley Poynton said, it did not necessarily see the play as representing the correct asset nor the correct timing to diversify away from Papua New Guinea.

The broker said it would be more appropriate for Oil Search to seek diversification opportunities after 2000, by when, assuming current exploration results continued, the company would have completed a critical phase in its maturation.
"In the interim, we do not see Oil Search making a grab for Discovery," it said.
